chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban, from Muhammad al-Wasiti, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not leave (saying) at the end of every prayer.'
'I seek Refuge for myself and for whatever my Lord has graced me with, with Allah, the One, the Last,' until you end it (Surah 112);
'and I seek Refuge for myself and whatever my Lord has graced me with, with the Lord of Al-Falaq,' until you end it (Surah 113);
'and I seek Refuge for myself and whatever my Lord has graced me with, with the Lord of the people,' until you end it (Surah 114).
ai.seo_question: What should be recited at the end of every prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the recitation of the three Quls as a recommended (mustahabb) act following obligatory prayers, emphasizing the protection of one's soul and bestowed blessings through divine refuge. In Shia tradition, this practice is viewed not merely as ritual completion but as a spiritual safeguard against external evils and internal distractions, reinforcing the believer's connection to Allah after the formalities of prayer. The chain of narration highlights the transmission of this practice through prominent Imami scholars, underscoring its authenticity and widespread acceptance in early Shia jurisprudence.
